To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

calpain and/or caspase- 3 inhibitors prevented glutamate-induced apoptosis and preserved normal activities of voltage-gated ion channels and ligand-gate ion channels (i.e., Na+ channels, kainate receptors, and N-methyl-D- aspartate receptors) in rat cortical neurons.
calpain and/or caspase- 3 inhibitors prevented glutamate-induced apoptotic neuronal death and maintained the normal activities of voltage- and ligand-gate ion channels in rat cortical neurons.
inhibition of calpain and/or caspase- 3 prevented neuronal death and preserved electrophysiologically important ion channels in rat cortical neurons following glutamatergic injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel neuroprotective agents that prevent glutamate-induced apoptosis and preserve electrophysiologically important ion channels in cortical neurons.

the mechanisms of glutamate-induced apoptotic death in cortical neurons and with the efficacy of calpains and caspases as potential targets in preventing apoptotic death in traumatic brain injury and in neurodegenerative disorders such as Huntington's disease.
the mechanisms of neuronal death and dysfunction following brain trauma and neurodegeneratives disease.
